{{Short description|Mathematics concept}}
In [[mathematics]], and particularly [[convex analysis]], the '''lower convex envelope''' <math>\breve f</math> of a [[real number|real]]-valued [[function (mathematics)|function]] <math>f</math> defined on a [[vector space]] <math>V</math> is defined [[pointwise]] as the [[supremum]] of all [[convex function]]s that lie under that function, i.e.<ref name=dacorogna/>

<math display=block>
\breve f (x) = \sup\{ g(x) \mid g \text{ is convex and } g \leq f \text{ over } V \}.
</math>

The lower convex envelope coincides with the [[biconjugate]] <math>f^{**}</math> of <math>f</math>, but can differ with the biconjugate when this definition is extended to functions whose domains are not the entire vector space or whose values are [[extended reals]], i.e., allowing <math>\pm\infty</math>. In such cases, one has the inequalities<ref name=dacorogna>{{citation
 | last = Dacorogna | first = Bernard
 | doi = 10.1007/978-0-387-55249-1
 | page = 35
 | publisher = Springer-Verlag
 | series = Applied Mathematical Sciences
 | title = Direct Methods in the Calculus of Variations
 | volume = 78
 | year = 2008}}</ref>
<math display=block>f^{**}(x)\le \breve f(x)\le f(x).</math>
